subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A wave-cut platform is formed as:
options: Sediment is deposited at a river mouth
A cliff retreats, leaving a rocky surface at its base
A stack collapses into a stump
questions.explain: As waves undercut and the cliff retreats, a flat rocky platform is left at the base.

questions.q: Mass movement at the coast, such as a landslide or slumping, occurs when:
options: Sediment is carried out to sea by waves
Material moves down a cliff under gravity, often after rain saturates it
questions.explain: Mass movement is the downhill movement of cliff material under gravity, often triggered by water saturation.

questions.q: When rocks knock together and become smaller and rounder, the process is:
questions.explain: Attrition wears rocks down as they collide, making them smaller and rounder.

questions.q: Natural raised banks of sediment along the edges of a river channel are called:
questions.explain: Levees are raised banks built up by repeated deposition during floods.

questions.q: A large ecosystem covering a wide area, such as tropical rainforest or tundra, is called a:
questions.explain: A biome is a very large-scale ecosystem, such as desert or rainforest, defined mainly by its climate and vegetation.

questions.q: An ox-bow lake forms when:
options: The neck of a meander is cut through and the loop is cut off
questions.explain: Erosion eventually cuts through a meander neck, leaving the loop as an ox-bow lake.

questions.q: In the rainforest, the few very tall trees that poke above the main canopy form the:
questions.explain: Emergents are the tallest trees, sometimes over 45m, that rise above the continuous canopy to reach maximum sunlight.

questions.q: Erosion caused by the sheer force of fast-moving water hitting and pushing into cracks in the bank is called:
questions.explain: Hydraulic action is the force of water compressing air in cracks, weakening rock.

questions.q: Which is a HUMAN cause of increased river flooding?
options: Building on floodplains and creating impermeable surfaces
questions.explain: Urbanisation adds impermeable surfaces and drains, speeding water into rivers.

questions.q: Which human activity is a major threat to global biodiversity?
questions.explain: Destroying habitats removes the homes of plants and animals, reducing the variety of life (biodiversity).

questions.q: An animal that eats only plants is best described as a:
questions.explain: A herbivore is a primary consumer that feeds only on plants (producers).

questions.q: Which biome is typically found in a broad band around the Equator?
questions.explain: Tropical rainforests are located close to the Equator, where high temperatures and heavy rainfall occur all year.

questions.q: What is the role of producers in a food chain?
options: They convert sunlight into energy by photosynthesis
They recycle nutrients into the soil
questions.explain: Producers such as green plants make their own food from sunlight through photosynthesis, forming the base of the food chain.

questions.q: How is an Arctic fox adapted to a cold environment?
options: Brightly coloured fur to attract a mate
Long limbs and large ears to lose heat
A thin coat to release heat
Thick white fur for warmth and camouflage in snow
questions.explain: The Arctic fox has thick fur for insulation that turns white in winter for camouflage, plus small ears to reduce heat loss.

questions.q: Which best explains why longshore drift moves sediment in a zig-zag?
options: Swash comes in at an angle but backwash drains straight down the beach
questions.explain: Wind-driven swash arrives at an angle while gravity pulls backwash straight down, moving sediment in a zig-zag.

questions.q: The coastal erosion process where waves throw pebbles against a cliff, wearing it away, is:
questions.explain: Abrasion occurs as waves hurl sediment against the cliff, grinding it away.

questions.q: Why does deforestation in a drainage basin increase flood risk?
options: Less interception and infiltration means water reaches the river faster
questions.explain: Removing trees cuts interception and infiltration, so rain runs quickly into the river, raising flood risk.

questions.q: Which of these is an opportunity provided by a hot desert environment?
questions.explain: The intense, reliable sunshine of hot deserts makes them ideal for generating solar power.

questions.q: Dissolved minerals carried invisibly in the water are transported by:
questions.explain: In solution, dissolved load is carried chemically within the water.

questions.q: Which adaptation helps a cactus survive in a hot desert?
options: Broad, flat leaves to catch rain
A thick, waxy stem to store water
questions.explain: A cactus stores water in its thick, waxy stem and has spines instead of leaves to reduce water loss.

questions.q: A long ridge of sand or shingle joined to the land at one end and projecting into the sea is a:
questions.explain: A spit is a depositional ridge attached to the coast at one end, formed by longshore drift.

questions.q: Managed retreat (coastal realignment) involves:
options: Allowing low-value land to flood and the coastline to move back
questions.explain: Managed retreat lets the sea flood low-value land, creating natural defences like salt marsh.
